title: Nothing sweeter than love (III.5)
hookLine: love is swift, sincere, patient, brave
tomorrow: can losing the argument actually bring you peace?

lines: TEN AT NIGHT, KEYS IN HAND.
cards: Ten at night. A kitchen. Someone's mom gets off the phone and says it plainly: your grandmother's having surgery next week, visit after, when she's settled.
The girl at the counter already has the car keys in her hand. Her thumb is on the group chat, half a message typed: should i just go now? Is that too much?
She's standing there, keys in one hand, phone in the other, and the cursor is blinking.

teach.b: The Imitation of Christ has a chapter for that blinking cursor. Book three is mostly a quiet talk between Christ and a disciple, and in its fifth chapter the disciple suddenly breaks into something like a song.
Love is a great thing, it says. It makes every heavy thing light and carries a burden without being burdened.
Then a run of nothings: nothing sweeter than love, nothing stronger, nothing higher, nothing wider, nothing fuller or better, in heaven or on earth. In the Latin, nihil dulcius est amore. Why?

teach.h: BORN OF GOD, RESTING IN GOD.
teach.b: Because love is born of God, the chapter says, and can't rest anywhere but in God. Then it shows how love moves. The lover flies, runs and rejoices.
Tired, it isn't worn out. Pressed, it isn't crushed. Like a living flame, it pushes upward.
And then the portrait, a list of what love is.
Here's the detail to tell someone tonight: the very first word on that list is swift. Before sincere, before patient, before faithful and brave, the Imitation puts speed.
Love doesn't wait until it has done the math. So the girl in the kitchen gets her answer. Patience is on the list too, and she can still respect her mom's worry.
But love, here, leans toward the door.

how: Catholics make short acts of love, prayers telling God of their love, and the Church teaches that love of God and love of neighbor belong together, lived out in the works of mercy.

games.q: what does “nothing sweeter than love” mean?
o: a sweet treat shared on a feast day
love from God that makes the heavy light

games.q: inside the song — tap the pairs.
p: of God, and rests only in God
the first word on the list

s: "nothing sweeter than love" in the Imitation is about romance
it's love born of God, which rests only in God and makes the heavy light.
the Imitation's list of what love is starts with swift
swift comes before sincere, patient, faithful and brave.
the chapter says love only tries what it knows it can do
love tries more than it can, the chapter says, and counts no effort.

games.q: your friend's dad lost his job today. you could text tonight, or wait and find the perfect thing to say this weekend. what would the Imitation's list lean toward?
o: text tonight, even a short line; love on the list is swift.
wait for the weekend; love is patient, so timing doesn't matter.
say nothing unless he asks; love never seeks itself.
games.why: patient and never seeking itself are on the list too, but the list starts with swift. love doesn't wait to do the math.

practice: Pick up your phone and think of one person who would be glad to hear from you right now. Send them one short line before you can weigh whether it's worth it.
Then set the phone face down and stay with them in mind for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Nothing sweeter than love. The Imitation's song: love born of God makes the heavy light, and the first thing it is, is swift.

orig.note: Latin, Imitation III.5: love is swift, the first word of the chapter's portrait of love.

carryVoice: Your line: nothing sweeter. And on the Imitation's list, love runs before it walks. See you tomorrow.
